key_insight: VGGT-Ω demonstrates that feed-forward 3D reconstruction quality scales predictably with model and data size; by scaling architecture and training at unprecedented scale, it achieves substantial gains in accuracy, efficiency, and dynamic-scene capability.
problem_solved: Brings reconstruction accuracy and geometry-awareness closer to traditional optimization-based methods while preserving the speed of feed-forward models, and extends robust reconstruction to both static and dynamic scenes at practical inference speeds.
method: Scale up the VGGT architecture (capacity and efficiency-focused blocks) to exploit predictable model-size scaling laws.
Train on much larger and more diverse datasets (data-scaling) with a tailored regimen to unlock improved generalization and dynamic-scene handling.
Produce geometry-aware intermediate features in a feed-forward pipeline to enable accurate reconstructions and useful embeddings for downstream tasks.
impact: Enables practitioners to trade compute and data for predictable improvements in reconstruction quality, obtaining near-optimization accuracy with much faster inference and versatile geometry-aware features for downstream applications like mapping, AR/VR, and robotics.
visual_elements: Scaling plot: model size / dataset size on x-axis vs reconstruction quality (metric) on y-axis showing predictable law
Before/after visualizations: side-by-side reconstructions of the same static and dynamic scenes comparing baseline VGGT and VGGT-Ω
Architecture diagram: feed-forward pipeline highlighting geometry-aware feature blocks and scaled capacity
Performance chart: latency vs accuracy (or FLOPs vs IoU/Chamfer) to illustrate efficiency gains
paper_authors: Jianyuan Wang, Minghao Chen, Shangzhan Zhang, Nikita Karaev, Johannes Schönberger
